messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The current bug report describes that JXPath automatically trims leading and trailing spaces from string values retrieved from XML elements, but it is expected to preserve those spaces.

The failing test `testPreserveJDOM()` calls `doTest("preserve", DocumentContainer.MODEL_JDOM, " foo ");` where `" foo "` has leading and trailing spaces which should be preserved when reading the XML content using JXPath.

Looking at the test method `doTest(String id, String model, String expectedValue)`, it creates a JXPathContext with a DocumentContainer created for the specified model (JDOM in this case), then asserts that the value obtained via XPath expression matches the expected value including spaces.

Inside the DocumentContainer constructor, it simply stores the URL and model without modification, so no trimming is done there.

Key inspection is at `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` which attempts to extract the string value for the XML node when the XML model is JDOM. It distinguishes node types:
- For `Element` nodes, it calls `((Element) node).getTextTrim()`.
- For `Comment` nodes, it trims the comment text explicitly.
- For `Text`, `CDATA` nodes, it also calls `getTextTrim()`.
- For `ProcessingInstruction` nodes, it trims the data string.

The critical method used for `Element`, `Text`, and `CDATA` nodes is `getTextTrim()`. This method by JDOM's design trims the text content, effectively removing any leading and trailing spaces. Hence, when JXPath retrieves values, the spaces are getting trimmed at this point.

This matches exactly the bug described: input XML like `<value> 12324 56</value>` turns into a trimmed string `"12324 56"`, not `" 12324 56"` as expected.

Thus, the root cause is that `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` uses the trimming method `getTextTrim()` on text-containing nodes, which forcibly removes leading/trailing whitespace, leading to unexpected trimming of string values retrieved by JXPath.

The fix would involve changing how the text value is retrieved to preserve the whitespace, probably by using a method that returns the raw text content without trimming.

No recent bug reports are relevant or contradictory to this diagnosis.

Recommendation for the fix location would be `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()`.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug report states that JXPath trims string values when retrieving XML content, removing leading and trailing spaces, contrary to expectations. The failing test calls `doTest("preserve", DocumentContainer.MODEL_JDOM, " foo ")`, which expects the spaces to be preserved.

Examining the `doTest` method, it uses a `JXPathContext` over a `DocumentContainer` set up with the JDOM model and fetches textual content at an XPath address. The key method for fetching text in the JDOM model is `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()`. In this method, when the node is an `Element`, it calls `getTextTrim()` on the JDOM Element, which trims whitespace. Similarly, for `Text` and `CDATA` nodes, it calls `getTextTrim()`. For `Comment` and `ProcessingInstruction` nodes, the code explicitly trims the text. 

This consistent use of `getTextTrim()` and explicit trimming leads to removal of leading and trailing whitespace in all these node types. This matches the observed behavior in the bug report.

Therefore, the root cause is that `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` uses the `getTextTrim()` method and explicit trimming calls that remove spaces, causing JXPath to not preserve whitespace in string values. 

To fix the bug, `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` should be changed to retrieve raw text values without trimming so that leading and trailing spaces are preserved as expected.

Suggested fix location:
- `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()`
